verses.1:1: The word of the Lord which came to Hosea, son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah and Jotham and Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam, son of Joash, king of Israel.
verses.1:2: The beginning of the word of the Lord through Hosea. And the Lord said to Hosea, "Go, take for yourself a wife of harlotry and children of harlotry, because the land will surely commit great harlotry, turning away from following the Lord."
verses.1:3: So he went and took Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.
verses.1:4: And the Lord said to him, "Call his name Jezreel, because in yet a little while I will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Judah, and I will bring to an end the kingdom of the house of Israel;
verses.1:5: and it shall come to pass in that day that I will shatter the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel."
verses.1:6: And she conceived again and bore a daughter. And He said to him, "Call her name 'Not Shown Mercy,' because I will no longer continue to show mercy to the house of Israel, but rather I will surely set Myself in opposition to them.
verses.1:7: But I will show mercy to the sons and will save them by the Lord their God; and I will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by war, nor by horses, nor by horsemen."
verses.1:8: And she weaned Not Shown Mercy, and conceived again and bore a son.
verses.1:9: And He said, "Call his name 'Not My People,' because you are not My people, and I am not yours."
verses.2:1: And the number of the sons of Israel was as the sand of the sea, which shall not be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass that in the place where it was said to them, "You are not My people," they also shall be called sons of the living God.
verses.2:2: And the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel shall be gathered together, and they shall appoint for themselves one ruler, and they shall go up out of the land; for great is the day of Jezreel.
verses.2:3: Say to your brother, "My People," and to your sister, "Shown Mercy."
verses.2:4: Contend against your mother, contend, for she is not My wife, and I am not her husband; and I will remove her harlotry from My presence, and her adultery from between her breasts,
verses.2:5: so that I may strip her naked and restore her as on the day of her birth; and I will make her desolate, and set her as a waterless land, and slay her with thirst.
verses.2:6: And I will by no means show mercy to her children, for they are children of harlotry.
verses.2:7: For their mother has committed harlotry; she who bore them has acted shamefully. For she said, "I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread and my water, and my garments and my linens, my oil and all things that are fitting for me."
verses.2:8: Therefore, behold, I hedge up her way with thorns, and I will wall up the ways, and she shall by no means find her path.
verses.2:9: And she shall pursue her lovers, and shall by no means overtake them; and she shall seek them, and shall by no means find them. Then she shall say, "I will go and return to my former husband, for it was better for me then than now."
verses.2:10: And she did not know that I gave her the grain and the wine and the oil, and multiplied silver for her; yet she made things of silver and gold for Baal.
verses.2:11: Therefore I will turn back and recover My grain in its season and My wine in its appointed time, and I will take away My garments and My linens, so that they may not cover her nakedness.
verses.2:12: And now I will uncover her uncleanness in the sight of her lovers, and no one shall by any means deliver her out of My hand.
verses.2:13: And I will turn away all her gladness, her feasts, and her new moons, and her Sabbaths, and all her solemn assemblies.
verses.2:14: And I will lay waste her vine and her fig trees, of which she said, "These are my wages that my lovers have given me." And I will make them a testimony, and the wild beasts of the field, and the birds of the heaven, and the creeping things of the earth shall devour them.
verses.2:15: And I will take vengeance upon her for the days of the Baalim, in which she offered sacrifice to them, and adorned herself with her earrings and her necklaces, and went after her lovers, but forgot Me, says the Lord.
verses.2:16: Therefore, behold, I will cause her to wander, and I will set her as a wilderness, and I will speak to her heart,
verses.2:17: and I will give her possessions to her from there, and the Valley of Achor to open her understanding; and she shall be humbled there according to the days of her infancy, and according to the days of her coming up out of the land of Egypt.
verses.2:18: And it shall come to pass in that day, says the Lord, that she shall call Me, "My Husband," and shall no longer call Me, "Baalim."
verses.2:19: And I will remove the names of the Baalim from her mouth, and their names shall by no means be remembered anymore.
verses.2:20: And I will make a covenant for them in that day with the wild beasts of the field, and with the birds of the heaven, and the creeping things of the earth; and I will shatter bow and sword and war from the earth, and I will cause you to dwell in hope.
verses.2:21: And I will betroth you to Myself forever; and I will betroth you to Myself in righteousness and in judgment, and in mercy and in compassions,
verses.2:22: and I will betroth you to Myself in faithfulness, and you shall know the Lord.
verses.2:23: And it shall come to pass in that day, says the Lord, that I will hear the heaven, and it shall hear the earth,
verses.2:24: and the earth shall hear the grain and the wine and the oil, and they shall hear Jezreel.
verses.2:25: And I will sow her for Myself upon the earth, and I will love Not Loved; and I will say to Not My People, "You are My people," and he shall say, "You are the Lord my God."
verses.3:1: And the Lord said to me, "Go again and love a woman who loves evil things and is an adulteress, even as God loves the sons of Israel, though they look to strange gods and love cakes with raisins."
verses.3:2: So I hired her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver, and a homer of barley, and a nebel of wine.
verses.3:3: And I said to her, "Many days you shall abide for me; and you shall by no means commit harlotry, nor shall you belong to any man; and so also shall I be for you."
verses.3:4: For many days the sons of Israel shall abide without a king, and without a prince, and without sacrifice, and without an altar, and without a priesthood, and without manifestations.
verses.3:5: And afterward the sons of Israel shall return and seek the Lord their God and David their king; and they shall stand in awe of the Lord and of His good things in the last days.
verses.4:1: Hear the word of the Lord, O sons of Israel, for the Lord has a judgment against those who dwell in the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land;
verses.4:2: cursing and lying and murder and theft and adultery have been poured out upon the land, and they mingle bloodshed upon bloodshed.
verses.4:3: Therefore the land shall mourn, and shall be diminished together with all who dwell in it, with the wild beasts of the field, and with the creeping things of the earth, and with the birds of heaven; and the fish of the sea shall fail,
verses.4:4: so that no one may contend in judgment, nor anyone reprove. Yet My people are like a priest who is spoken against,
verses.4:5: and he shall grow weak by day, and a prophet shall grow weak with you; to the night I have likened your mother.
verses.4:6: My people have been likened to one who has no knowledge; because you have rejected knowledge, I also will reject you from serving as priest to Me; and you have forgotten the law of your God, and I also will forget your children.
verses.4:7: According to their multitude, so they sinned against Me; I will turn their glory into dishonor.
verses.4:8: They shall eat the sins of My people, and in their iniquities they shall take their souls.
verses.4:9: And it shall be: as with the people, so also with the priest; and I will avenge his ways upon him, and his counsels I will repay to him.
verses.4:10: And they shall eat, and shall by no means be filled; they committed harlotry, and shall by no means prosper, because they have forsaken the Lord to keep
verses.4:11: harlotry. And the heart of My people has received wine and strong drink;
verses.4:12: they inquired by omens, and by his rods they declared to him; by a spirit of harlotry they were led astray, and they committed harlotry away from their God.
verses.4:13: Upon the summits of the mountains they sacrificed, and upon the hills they made offerings, beneath an oak and a white poplar and an overshadowing tree, because the shelter is good. Therefore your daughters shall commit harlotry, and your brides shall commit adultery;
verses.4:14: and I will by no means visit punishment upon your daughters when they commit harlotry, nor upon your brides when they commit adultery; for they themselves mingled with the harlots, and offered sacrifices with the initiated ones, and the people who had understanding became entangled with a harlot.
verses.4:15: But as for you, O Israel, do not be ignorant; and O Judah, do not enter into Gilgal, and do not go up to the house of On, and do not swear by the living Lord.
verses.4:16: Because like a frenzied heifer, Israel has run wild; now the Lord shall pasture them like a lamb in a broad place.
verses.4:17: A partner with idols, Ephraim has set stumbling blocks for himself;
verses.4:18: he has chosen Canaanites; committing harlotry, they have utterly given themselves to harlotry; they have loved dishonor out of her arrogance.
verses.4:19: You are a whirlwind in her wings, and they shall be put to shame because of their altars.
verses.5:1: Hear these things, O priests, and give heed, O house of Israel, and O house of the king, give ear, because the judgment is against you; for you have become a snare to the watchtower, and like a net spread out upon Tabor,
verses.5:2: which those who hunt the prey have set fast. Yet I am your discipliner;
verses.5:3: I have known Ephraim, and Israel is not absent from Me; because now Ephraim has committed harlotry, Israel has been defiled.
verses.5:4: They did not give their counsels to return to their God, for a spirit of harlotry is in them, and they have not known the Lord.
verses.5:5: And the arrogance of Israel shall be humbled to his face, and Israel and Ephraim shall grow weak in their iniquities, and Judah also shall grow weak with them.
verses.5:6: With sheep and calves they shall go to seek out the Lord, and they shall by no means find Him, for He has turned aside from them;
verses.5:7: because they have forsaken the Lord, for strange children were born to them; now the blight shall devour them and their allotments.
verses.5:8: Sound the trumpet upon the hills, make a loud cry upon the high places, proclaim in the house of On: Benjamin is astounded,
verses.5:9: Ephraim has become a desolation in the days of reproof; among the tribes of Israel I have shown faithful things.
verses.5:10: The rulers of Judah have become like those who shift boundaries; upon them I will pour out My fury like water.
verses.5:11: Ephraim has oppressed his adversary, he has trampled down justice, because he began to walk after vain things.
verses.5:12: And I am like turmoil to Ephraim, and like a goad to the house of Judah.
verses.5:13: And Ephraim saw his sickness, and Judah his pain; and Ephraim went to the Assyrians and sent ambassadors to King Jareim; yet he was not able to heal you, and pain shall by no means cease from you.
verses.5:14: Because I am like a panther to Ephraim, and like a lion to the house of Judah; and I will seize and depart, and I will carry off, and there shall be no one who delivers.
verses.5:15: I will depart and return to My place, until they are brought to ruin and seek My face. In their affliction they shall rise early to Me, saying,
verses.6:1: "Let us go and return to the Lord our God, for He has seized, and He will heal us; He will strike, and He will bind us up;
verses.6:2: He will make us whole after two days; on the third day we shall rise up,
verses.6:3: and we shall live before Him, and we shall know; we shall press on to know the Lord; like the ready dawn we shall find Him, and He shall come to us like rain, early and late rain for the earth."
verses.6:4: What shall I do to you, O Ephraim? What shall I do to you, O Judah? For your mercy is like a morning cloud, and like the early dew that passes away.
verses.6:5: Therefore I have mowed down your prophets; I have slain them by the word of My mouth, and My judgment shall go forth like light.
verses.6:6: Because I desire mercy rather than sacrifice, and the knowledge of God rather than whole burnt offerings.
verses.6:7: Yet they are like a man who transgresses a covenant; there Gilead despised Me, a city
verses.6:9: and your strength is that of a robber; priests hid the way, they murdered Shechem, because they practiced lawlessness
verses.6:10: in the house of Israel. I saw horrible things there, the harlotry of Ephraim; Israel and Judah were defiled. Begin to gather the vintage for yourself
verses.6:11: when I restore the captivity of My people,
verses.7:1: When I heal Israel, then the iniquity of Ephraim shall be revealed, and the wickedness of Samaria, because they have practiced falsehood; and a thief shall come in to him, a robber stripping along his road,
verses.7:2: so that they may sing together like those who sing in their heart. I have remembered all their wicked deeds; now their own counsels have surrounded them; they have come before My face.
verses.7:3: With their wicked deeds they have gladdened kings, and princes with their falsehoods.
verses.7:4: All of them are adulterers, like an oven burning for baking with scorching heat from the flame, from the kneading of the dough until it is leavened.
verses.7:5: In the days of your kings, the princes began to rage from wine; he stretched out his hand with pestilent men.
verses.7:6: For their hearts were kindled like an oven; while they were breaking down, all the night Ephraim was filled with sleep; morning came, and it was kindled like a brightness of fire.
verses.7:7: All of them grew hot like an oven, and they devoured their judges; all their kings have fallen; there was not one among them who called upon Me.
verses.7:8: Ephraim mingled himself among his peoples; Ephraim became a cake baked in the ashes, not turned.
verses.7:9: Strangers have devoured his strength, yet he did not know it; and gray hairs have sprouted upon him, and he did not know it.
verses.7:10: And the arrogance of Israel shall be humbled to his face, yet they did not return to the Lord their God, nor did they seek Him diligently in all these things.
verses.7:11: And Ephraim was like a senseless dove, having no heart; he called upon Egypt, and they went to the Assyrians.
verses.7:12: Wherever they go, I will cast My net upon them; like the birds of heaven I will bring them down; I will chasten them at the report of their affliction.
verses.7:13: Woe to them, because they have leaped away from Me! Wretched are they, because they have acted ungodly toward Me! Though I redeemed them, yet they spoke falsehoods against Me.
verses.7:14: And their hearts did not cry out to Me; rather, they wailed upon their beds; for grain and wine they slashed themselves.
verses.7:15: They were instructed by Me, and I strengthened their arms, yet against Me they devised evil things.
verses.7:16: They turned away to nothing; they became like a bent bow; their princes shall fall by the sword because of the unruliness of their tongue; this shall be their derision in the land of Egypt.
verses.8:1: Into their bosom as earth, like an eagle against the house of the Lord, because they have transgressed My covenant and gone against My law.
verses.8:2: They shall cry out to Me, "O God, we have known You."
verses.8:3: Because Israel has turned away from good things, they have pursued an enemy.
verses.8:4: They reigned for themselves, and not through Me; they ruled, and did not make it known to Me; of their silver and their gold they made idols for themselves, so that they might be utterly destroyed.
verses.8:5: Cast off your calf, O Samaria! My wrath is provoked against them; how long shall they be unable to be cleansed
verses.8:6: in Israel? For a craftsman made it, and it is not God; because your calf was leading astray, O Samaria.
verses.8:7: For they have sown wind-blighted things, and their destruction shall receive them—a sheaf having no strength to yield meal; and even if it should yield some, strangers shall devour it.
verses.8:8: Israel has been swallowed up; now he has become among the nations like a useless vessel.
verses.8:9: For they themselves have gone up to the Assyrians; Ephraim blossomed again by himself; they loved gifts,
verses.8:10: therefore they shall be delivered over among the nations. Now I will take them in, and they shall cease for a little while from anointing a king and princes.
verses.8:11: Because Ephraim has multiplied altars, beloved altars have become to him for sins.
verses.8:12: I will write down a multitude for him, yet My statutes were reckoned as strange things—the beloved altars.
verses.8:13: For if they offer a sacrifice and eat flesh, the Lord will not accept them; now He will remember their iniquities and punish their sins; they have returned to Egypt, and among the Assyrians they shall eat unclean things.
verses.8:14: And Israel has forgotten Him who made him, and they have built shrines; and Judah has multiplied walled cities; and I will send forth fire into his cities, and it shall devour their foundations.
verses.9:1: Do not rejoice, O Israel, nor be glad like the peoples; for you have played the harlot away from your God, you have loved gifts upon every threshing floor of grain.
verses.9:2: The threshing floor and the winepress did not know them, and the wine has deceived them.
verses.9:3: They did not dwell in the land of the Lord; Ephraim has dwelt in Egypt, and among the Assyrians they shall eat unclean things.
verses.9:4: They did not pour out wine to the Lord, nor were they pleasing to Him; their sacrifices are like bread of mourning to them; all who eat them shall be defiled, because their loaves are for their own souls; they shall not enter into the house of the Lord.
verses.9:5: What will you do in the days of the solemn assembly, and in the day of the feast of the Lord?
verses.9:6: Therefore, behold, they go forth from the misery of Egypt, and Memphis shall receive them, and Machmas shall bury them; as for their silver, destruction shall inherit it; thorns shall be in the tents.
verses.9:7: The days of vengeance have come, the days of your recompense have come, and Israel shall be afflicted like the prophet who is beside himself, the man who is spirit-borne; by the multitude of your iniquities, your madness has been multiplied.
verses.9:8: Ephraim is a watchman with God; a prophet is a crooked snare upon all his ways; they have planted madness in the house of God.
verses.9:9: They have become corrupted as in the days of the hill; He will remember their iniquities; He will punish their sins.
verses.9:10: Like a cluster of grapes in the wilderness I found Israel, and like an early watchman on a fig tree I saw their fathers; they went in to Baal-peor, and became estranged in shame, and the abominable ones became like the beloved ones.
verses.9:11: Ephraim has flown away like a bird—their glories from births and birth pangs and conceptions;
verses.9:12: for even if they rear their children, they shall be made childless from among men; for indeed woe is to them; My flesh is from them.
verses.9:13: Ephraim, just as they presented their children for prey, so Ephraim must bring forth his children to slaughter.
verses.9:14: Give to them, O Lord—what will You give to them? A childless womb and dry breasts.
verses.9:15: All their wicked deeds are in Gilgal, for there I hated them because of the wickedness of their practices; I will drive them out of My house; I will no longer continue to love them; all their princes are disobedient.
verses.9:16: Ephraim is afflicted; he is dried up at his roots; he shall no longer bear fruit; for even if they bear children, I will slay the cherished ones of their womb.
verses.9:17: God will cast them away, because they did not listen to Him; and they shall be wanderers among the nations.
verses.10:1: Israel is a vine rich in branches; its fruit is abundant. According to the multitude of its fruits he multiplied altars; according to the good things of his land he built pillars.
verses.10:2: They have divided their hearts; now they shall be destroyed. He Himself will tear down their altars; their pillars shall come to ruin.
verses.10:3: For now they shall say, "We have no king, because we did not fear the Lord. And what will the king do for us,
verses.10:4: speaking words of false pretexts?" He will make a covenant; judgment shall spring up like wild grass upon the barren ground of a field.
verses.10:5: The inhabitants of Samaria shall sojourn for the calf of the house of On, because its people mourned over it; and just as they provoked it, they shall rejoice over its glory, because it has been carried away into exile from it.
verses.10:6: And having bound it, they carried it away to the Assyrians as gifts to King Jarim; Ephraim shall receive it as a gift, and Israel shall be put to shame in his counsel.
verses.10:7: Samaria has cast off her king like a dry twig upon the face of the water.
verses.10:8: And the altars of On, the sins of Israel, shall be taken away; thorns and thistles shall grow up upon their altars; and they shall say to the mountains, "Cover us," and to the hills, "Fall upon us."
verses.10:9: From the time of the hills Israel has sinned; there they stood. War shall by no means overtake them on the hill against the children of unrighteousness
verses.10:10: to chasten them; and peoples shall be gathered against them when they are chastened for their two iniquities.
verses.10:11: Ephraim is a heifer taught to love contention, yet I will come upon the fairness of her neck; I will ride upon Ephraim; I will pass over Judah in silence; Jacob shall prevail for himself.
verses.10:12: Sow for yourselves in righteousness; reap for the fruit of life; light for yourselves the light of knowledge; seek the Lord until the produce of righteousness comes to us.
verses.10:13: Why have you passed over ungodliness in silence, reaped its iniquities, and eaten false fruit? Because you have trusted in your sins, in the multitude of your strength,
verses.10:14: destruction shall rise up among your people, and all your fortified places shall vanish away. Just as Prince Salaman from the house of Jeroboam, in the days of war they dashed mother upon children to the ground,
verses.10:15: so I will do to you, O house of Israel, because of the unrighteousness of your evil deeds.
verses.11:1: At dawn they were cast off; the king of Israel has been cast off. For Israel was a child, and I loved him, and out of Egypt I called his children.
verses.11:2: Just as I called them, so they departed from My presence; they sacrificed to the Baals and burned incense to carved images.
verses.11:3: And I bound the feet of Ephraim; I took him up upon My arm; they did not know that I healed them.
verses.11:4: In the corruption of men I stretched them out with the bonds of My love, and I will be to them like a man striking upon his cheeks; and I will look toward him; I will prevail over him.
verses.11:5: Ephraim dwelt in Egypt, and Assyria itself was his king, because he was unwilling to turn back.
verses.11:6: And he grew weak by the sword in his cities, and ceased in his hands; and they shall eat from their own counsels.
verses.11:7: And his people hang suspended from his dwelling; and God shall be wrathful against his precious things, and He shall by no means exalt him.
verses.11:8: How shall I treat you, O Ephraim? Shall I shield you, O Israel? What shall I make of you? I will set you like Admah and like Zeboiim. My heart is turned within at once; My remorse is deeply troubled;
verses.11:9: I will by no means act according to the fierceness of My wrath; I will by no means abandon Ephraim to be blotted out; for I am God and not man, the Holy One in your midst, and I will not enter into a city.
verses.11:10: I will walk after the Lord; like a lion He shall roar, for He Himself shall bellow, and the children of the waters shall be astonished.
verses.11:11: They shall fly forth like a bird out of Egypt, and like a dove from the land of the Assyrians; and I will restore them to their houses, says the Lord.
verses.12:1: Ephraim has surrounded Me with falsehood, and the house of Israel and Judah with ungodliness. Now God has known them, and they shall be called a holy people of God.
verses.12:2: But Ephraim is an evil spirit; he pursued the scorching wind all the day long. He multiplied empty and vain things, and made a covenant with the Assyrians, and carried oil in trade to Egypt.
verses.12:3: And the Lord has a judgment against Judah, to punish Jacob according to his ways; and according to his practices He will repay him.
verses.12:4: In the womb he supplanted his brother, and in his labors he prevailed with God;
verses.12:5: indeed, he prevailed with an angel and proved strong. They wept and pleaded with Me; in the house of On they found Me, and there it was spoken to them.
verses.12:6: And the Lord God Almighty shall be his memorial.
verses.12:7: Therefore you shall return in your God; observe mercy and judgment, and draw near to your God continually.
verses.12:8: As for Canaan, in his hand is a balance of unrighteousness; he has loved to oppress.
verses.12:9: And Ephraim said, "Indeed, I have become rich; I have found relief for myself." All his labors shall not be found for him because of the iniquities which he has sinned.
verses.12:10: Yet I, the Lord your God, brought you up out of the land of Egypt; I will again cause you to dwell in tents, as in the days of the feast.
verses.12:11: And I will speak to the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and by the hands of the prophets I was represented.
verses.12:12: If Gilead does not exist, then the rulers sacrificing in Gilead were false, and their altars are like tortoises upon the barren ground of a field.
verses.12:13: And Jacob withdrew to the plain of Syria, and Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept watch.
verses.12:14: And by a prophet the Lord brought Israel up out of the land of Egypt, and by a prophet he was preserved.
verses.12:15: Ephraim provoked fury and stirred up wrath; and his blood shall be poured out upon him, and the Lord will repay his reproach to him.
verses.13:1: According to the word of Ephraim, he himself received ordinances in Israel, and he assigned them to Baal and died.
verses.13:2: And they continued to sin, and made for themselves a molten image from their silver according to the likeness of idols, the works of craftsmen completed for them; they themselves say, "Sacrifice men, for calves have failed."
verses.13:3: Therefore they shall be like a morning cloud and like the early dew that departs, like chaff blown away from a threshing floor and like vapor from tears.
verses.13:4: Yet I am the Lord your God, who establishes the heaven and creates the earth, whose hands created all the host of heaven, and I did not show them to you to walk after them; and I brought you up out of the land of Egypt, and you shall know no God besides Me, and there is no savior apart from Me.
verses.13:5: I shepherded you in the wilderness, in an uninhabited land,
verses.13:6: according to their pastures; and they were filled to satisfaction, and their hearts were lifted up; for this reason they forgot Me.
verses.13:7: And I will be to them like a panther, and like a leopard along the road of the Assyrians;
verses.13:8: I will meet them like a bear in distress, and I will tear open the enclosure of their heart, and whelps of the forest shall devour them there; wild beasts of the field shall tear them apart.
verses.13:9: In your destruction, O Israel, who will help?
verses.13:10: Where is this king of yours? And let him deliver you in all your cities; let him judge you, of whom you said, "Give me a king and a ruler."
verses.13:11: And I gave you a king in My anger, and I held back in My wrath.
verses.13:12: A bundle of iniquity is Ephraim; his sin is hidden away;
verses.13:13: birth pangs like those of a woman in labor shall come upon him. This is your wise son, for he shall by no means stand firm in the crushing of children.
verses.13:14: From the hand of Hades I will deliver them, and from death I will redeem them. Where is your penalty, O death? Where is your sting, O Hades? Comfort is hidden from My eyes,
verses.13:15: because this one shall cause division among brethren. The Lord shall bring a scorching wind from the wilderness upon him, and He shall dry up his veins and lay waste his springs; He Himself shall parch his land and all his desirable vessels.
verses.14:1: Samaria shall be laid waste, because she has stood against her God; they themselves shall fall by the sword, and their nursing infants shall be dashed to the ground, and their women with child shall be ripped open.
verses.14:2: Return, O Israel, to the Lord your God, for you have become weak in your iniquities.
verses.14:3: Take words with you and return to the Lord your God; speak to Him, so that you may not receive iniquity, and that you may receive good things, and we will render the fruit of our lips.
verses.14:4: Assyria shall by no means save us; we will not mount upon a horse; never again will we say, "Our gods," to the works of our hands; he who is in You shall have mercy on the orphan.
verses.14:5: I will heal their dwellings; I will love them openly, for he has turned away My anger from him.
verses.14:6: I will be like dew to Israel; he shall blossom like a lily, and cast forth his roots like Lebanon;
verses.14:7: his branches shall go forth, and he shall be like a fruitful olive tree, and his fragrance like that of Lebanon.
verses.14:8: They shall return and dwell under his shelter; they shall live and be intoxicated with grain; and a vine shall blossom as his memorial, like the wine of Lebanon.
verses.14:9: As for Ephraim, what has he any longer to do with idols? I have humbled him, and I will strengthen him; I am like a dense juniper tree; from Me your fruit is found.
verses.14:10: Who is wise, and shall understand these things? Or discerning, and shall recognize them? For the ways of the Lord are straight, and the righteous shall walk in them, but the ungodly shall become weak in them.

notes.1:4: The Greek text reads "the house of Judah" rather than "the house of Jehu" as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.1:6: The Greek translates the daughter's symbolic name as "Not Shown Mercy" and concludes the verse with "I will surely set Myself in opposition to them" rather than a denial of forgiveness.
notes.1:7: The critical Greek text reads simply "the sons," omitting "of Judah" found in the Hebrew and some Greek manuscripts.
notes.2:1: Septuagint chapter 2 begins three verses earlier than most English Bibles (covering English 1:10–2:23) and opens with the past-tense verb "was" before shifting to the future.
notes.2:4: The Greek expresses the removal of harlotry in the first person, "I will remove her harlotry from My presence," rather than as a third-person exhortation.
notes.2:14: The Greek reads "a testimony" where the Hebrew has "a forest," and expands the clause to include the birds of the heaven and the creeping things of the earth.
notes.2:17: The Greek distinctively reads "her possessions," "to open her understanding" (rather than "a door of hope"), and "she shall be humbled."
notes.2:25: Here the Greek shifts from "mercy" (1:6; 2:3) to "love," reading "I will love Not Loved" (later echoed in Romans 9:25), and expands the final reply to "You are the Lord my God."
notes.3:1: The Greek describes the woman as one "who loves evil things" and reads "God" rather than the Lord in the comparison clause.
notes.3:2: A "homer" (Greek gomor) is a dry measure, and a "nebel" (Greek nebel) is a wineskin or jar measure of wine, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads a half-homer of barley.
notes.3:4: Where the Hebrew lists sacred pillar, ephod, and teraphim, the Greek reads "altar," "priesthood," and "manifestations" (the Septuagint term for the priestly Urim).
notes.4:5: Greek "likened" (also in 4:6) reflects reading the Hebrew root as "be like" rather than "destroy."
notes.4:11: The Greek syntax links "harlotry" to the end of 4:10 ("to keep harlotry") and reads "the heart of My people has received wine and strong drink."
notes.4:14: Greek "initiated ones" refers to devotees of pagan mystery rites, and unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text, the Greek describes the people as "having understanding" yet becoming entangled with a harlot.
notes.4:15: Greek "the house of On" (also in 5:8) renders the name as On rather than the Hebrew Beth-aven.
notes.5:1: Greek translates Hebrew Mizpah literally as "the watchtower" and uses the Greek form Itabyrion for Mount Tabor.
notes.5:7: Greek reads "the blight" (mildew or rust) rather than the Hebrew "new moon" or "month."
notes.5:8: Greek translates Gibeah and Ramah literally as "the hills" and "the high places," and concludes the verse with "Benjamin is astounded."
notes.5:13: Greek preserves the distinct name "King Jareim" (compare Hebrew Jareb or "the great king") and explicitly mentions "ambassadors."
notes.6:2: Greek reads "we shall rise up" rather than the Hebrew "He will raise us up," and places "and we shall live before Him" at the start of 6:3.
notes.6:7: Greek reads "like a man" rather than "like Adam" (or "at Adam"), and joins "Gilead, a city" to the verb "despised Me" before continuing into 6:8.
notes.6:8: Greek reads "troubling water" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "tracked with blood."
notes.6:10: Greek joins "and Judah" to the defilement of Israel and reads "Begin to gather the vintage for yourself," continuing directly into 6:11.
notes.7:2: The Septuagint reads "so that they may sing together like those who sing in their heart," diverging from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("they do not consider in their hearts").
notes.7:6: The Greek reads "Ephraim was filled with sleep," reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew consonants behind the Masoretic Text's "their baker sleeps."
notes.7:14: The Greek verb "slashed themselves" reflects an underlying reading referring to self-laceration in ritual mourning, distinct from the Masoretic Text's "assemble themselves."
notes.8:1: The Septuagint reads "Into their bosom as earth," diverging from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("Set the trumpet to your mouth") through a different reading of the Hebrew consonants.
notes.8:9: The Greek "blossomed again by himself" reflects a Hebrew root meaning "to flourish," whereas the Masoretic Text reads "a wild donkey alone by itself."
notes.8:10: The Greek reads "from anointing a king and princes," whereas the Masoretic Text refers to "the burden of the king of princes."
notes.9:6: The Septuagint preserves the proper name Machmas (Michmash) as the second burial site alongside Memphis, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "precious things" of silver.
notes.9:9: The Greek translates the Hebrew place name Gibeah literally as "the hill."
notes.9:10: The Greek reads "an early watchman on a fig tree" (using the same noun for "watchman" as in 9:8), where the Masoretic Text has "the first-ripe fruit on the fig tree."
notes.9:12: The Septuagint reads "My flesh is from them," reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants rendered in the Masoretic Text as "when I depart from them."
notes.9:13: The Greek renders "for prey" where the Masoretic Text reads "like Tyre," reflecting a closely similar Hebrew word.
notes.10:5: The Greek reads "sojourn" (where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "fear"), "the house of On" (for Beth-aven), and "provoked it" (where the Hebrew has "its priests").
notes.10:6: The Greek preserves the proper name Jarim (for Hebrew Jareb) and reads "in/as a gift" (where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "shame").
notes.10:11: The Greek renders two verbs differently from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, reading "love contention" (vs. "love to thresh") and "pass over Judah in silence" (vs. "Judah shall plow").
notes.10:14: The Greek names "Prince Salaman from the house of Jeroboam," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Shalman destroyed Beth-arbel."
notes.11:1: In the Septuagint, the opening clause ("At dawn they were cast off...") begins 11:1 rather than ending 10:15, and the final phrase reads "his children" rather than "My son" (as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text and Matt 2:15).
notes.11:3: The Greek verb synepodisa means "I bound the feet of," reflecting a distinct interpretation of the Hebrew root for "foot" (where the Masoretic Text reads "I taught Ephraim to walk").
notes.11:4: The Greek diverges from the Hebrew Masoretic Text throughout this verse, reading "in the corruption of men," "striking upon his cheeks," and "I will prevail over him."
notes.11:10: The Greek has first-person singular "I will walk" (vs. third-person plural in Hebrew) and "children of the waters" (for Hebrew "children from the west/sea").
notes.12:2: The Greek reads "an evil spirit," interpreting the Hebrew consonants for "feeds on wind" as "evil spirit."
notes.12:5: The Greek reads "in the house of On" (where the Hebrew has "Bethel") and shifts to third-person plural ("they wept... they found Me") with God speaking in the first person.
notes.12:12: The Greek reads "rulers sacrificing in Gilead" (vs. Hebrew "in Gilgal they sacrifice bulls") and compares their altars to "tortoises" (chelonai, vs. Hebrew "stone heaps").
notes.13:2: The Septuagint reads "Sacrifice men, for calves have failed," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text speaks of men who sacrifice kissing calves.
notes.13:3: The Septuagint literally reads "vapor from tears" (apo dakryon), a distinctive Greek reading compared with the Hebrew "smoke from a lattice."
notes.13:4: The Septuagint preserves an expanded declaration of the Lord as Creator of heaven, earth, and the heavenly host, emphasizing that Israel was not shown them in order to worship them.
notes.13:14: The Septuagint's rhetorical questions—"Where is your penalty, O death? Where is your sting, O Hades?"—closely underlie Paul's quotation in 1 Corinthians 15:55.
notes.14:1: Following Septuagint versification, chapter 14 opens with the oracle against Samaria (numbered 13:16 in the Hebrew Masoretic Text), advancing the verse numbers of the chapter by one.
notes.14:3: The Greek renders the clause as a purpose statement ("so that you may not receive iniquity") and concludes with "the fruit of our lips," a Septuagint expression echoed in Hebrews 13:15.
notes.14:4: The final clause ("he who is in You shall have mercy on the orphan") reflects the Septuagint's active verb and relative construction, portraying the one who abides in God as showing compassion.
notes.14:5: The Septuagint reads "dwellings" (katoikias) rather than the Hebrew "apostasy," and the Greek critical text uses a third-person singular verb ("for he has turned away My anger from him").
